title: SREV-013 relative symlink canonicalizer shape

mscc_symlink_shape.description: MS-FSCC symbolic-link reparse buffer permits a relative substitute name; either pathname may contain dot directory names; SubstituteNameLength is the only legal length source

input_buffer_invariant.description: File_CanonizePath treats relative_path as a length-bounded buffer of rel_path_len WCHARs and never reads past that bound

bounds_owner.description: Dot-segment detection uses explicit `i + 1 < rel_path_len` and `i + 2 < rel_path_len` checks before reading relative_path[i+1] or relative_path[i+2]

root_floor_invariant.description: root_floor is computed from absolute_path leading `\` or drive letter; parent traversal stops at root_floor and returns NULL if `..` would climb above it

fail_closed_invariant.description: File_SetReparsePoint fails closed when relative symlink canonicalization cannot produce an absolute path

runtime_matrix.description: Windows runtime gate: relative symlinks with normal, dot, and dotdot segments canonicalize correctly; one-character or excessive .. inputs fail closed

contracts: Relative symlink substitute name length is SubstituteNameLength bytes; no trailing NUL is guaranteed
File_CanonizePath uses unsigned index i bounded by `i < rel_path_len` for all reads
Multi-character dot patterns read relative_path[i+1] and relative_path[i+2] only when `i + 1 < rel_path_len` and `i + 2 < rel_path_len`
Parent traversal stops at root_floor; climbing above root_floor returns NULL
Output buffer size is (abs_path_len + rel_path_len + 1) * sizeof(WCHAR)
